resposta:
Com base na pesquisa realizada, aqui está a lista completa dos Secretários de Estado dos EUA no período de **início de 2018 até o fim de 2024**, incluindo secretários interinos (*acting*):

---

## Secretários de Estado dos EUA (2018–2024)

### 🔵 Rex Tillerson (secretário titular)
| Período | Detalhes |
|---------|----------|
| **Até 31 de março de 2018** | Último secretário nomeado por Donald Trump antes da transição. Estava no cargo desde fevereiro de 2017 e saiu em março de 2018 para se tornar CEO da Chevron. |

---

### 🟡 John J. Sullivan (secretário interino)
| Período | Detalhes |
|---------|----------|
| **1º de abril a 26 de abril de 2018** (25 dias) | Serviu como *acting Secretary of State* enquanto Mike Pompeo aguardava confirmação pelo Senado. Era diplomata de carreira. |

---

### 🔴 Mike Pompeo (secretário titular)
| Período | Detalhes |
|---------|----------|
| **26 de abril de 2018 a 20 de janeiro de 2021** (~2 anos e 9 meses) | Nomeado por Trump, foi confirmada pelo Senado em 23 de abril de 2018. Cumpriu praticamente toda a administração Trump. Renunciou em 20 de janeiro de 2021. |

---

### 🟡 Daniel Bennett Smith (secretário interino)
| Período | Detalhes |
|---------|----------|
| **20 a 26 de janeiro de 2021** (6 dias) | Dirigiu a Casa Branca temporariamente quando Pompeo renunciou de última hora na véspera da posse de Biden. Era diretor do Instituto de Serviços Estrangeiros. Foi substituído rapidamente por Antony Blinken. |

---

### 🔵 Antony Blinken (secretário titular)
| Período | Detalhes |
|---------|----------|
| **26 de janeiro de 2021 a 20 de janeiro de 2025** (~3 anos) | Nomeado por Joe Biden em fevereiro de 2021 (confirmado em 26 de janeiro). Cumprindo o restante do mandato de Biden, ficou no cargo durante **todo o período de 2021 a 2024**. Em 20 de janeiro de 2025, deixou o posto para a eleição de Donald Trump. |

---

## Resumo do período solicitado (2018–2024)

| # | Secretário | Tipo | Período |
|---|-----------|------|---------|
| 1 | **Rex Tillerson** | Titular | jan–mar 2018 |
| 2 | **John J. Sullivan** | Interino | abr 2018 (25 dias) |
| 3 | **Mike Pompeo** | Titular | abr 2018 – jan 2021 |
| 4 | **Daniel Bennett Smith** | Interino | jan 2021 (6 dias) |
| 5 | **Antony Blinken** | Titular | jan 2021 – dez 2024 (toda a segunda metade do período) |

**Total de transições:** 4 trocas no período, sendo 2 secretários interinos breves. A maior parte do tempo foi sob Pompeo (até jan/2021) e depois sob Blinken (por todo o resto do mandato de Biden e além).

> ⚠️ Observação: Não houve mudanças no cargo entre 2021 e dezembro de 2024, exceto pela breve passagem de Smith em janeiro de 2021. Portanto, os dois nomes principais que cobriram esse período foram **Pompeo (2018–jan 2021)** e **Blinken (jan 2021–dez 2024)**.

This is a **list of United States secretaries of state**.

## Secretaries of foreign affairs (1781–1789)

On January 10, 1780, the [Congress of the Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_the_Confederation "Congress of the Confederation") created the Department of Foreign Affairs.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_secretaries_of_state#cite_note-1)

On August 10, 1781, Congress selected [Robert R. Livingston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_R._Livingston "Robert R. Livingston"), a delegate from [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)"), as the first secretary for foreign affairs. Livingston was unable to take office until October 20, 1781. He served until June 4, 1783, and was succeeded by [Elias Boudinot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elias_Boudinot "Elias Boudinot"), who was succeeded by [John Jay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jay "John Jay") on December 21, 1784, who served until March 4, 1789, when the government under the [Articles of Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Articles_of_Confederation "Articles of Confederation") gave way to the government under the [Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_the_United_States "Constitution of the United States").

The office of secretary of foreign affairs and the Department of Foreign Affairs were reinstated by a law signed by [George Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington") on July 27, 1789. [John Jay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jay "John Jay") retained the post on an interim basis, pending the return of [Thomas Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson") from France.

## Secretaries of state

On September 15, 1789, before Jefferson could return to take the post, Washington signed into law another act which changed the name of the office from Secretary of Foreign Affairs to [Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State"), changed the name of the department to the [Department of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State"), and added several domestic powers and responsibilities to both the office of secretary and the department. [Thomas Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson") took office as the first secretary of state on March 22, 1790.

This is a list of United States secretaries of state by time in office. This is based on the difference between dates; if counted by number of calendar days all the figures would be one greater. [Cordell Hull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cordell_Hull "Cordell Hull") is the only person to have served as secretary of state for more than eight years. [Daniel Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Webster "Daniel Webster") and [James G. Blaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_G._Blaine "James G. Blaine") are the only secretaries of state to have ever served non-consecutive terms. [Warren Christopher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Christopher "Warren Christopher") served very briefly as acting secretary of state non-consecutively with his later tenure as full-fledged secretary of state. [Elihu B. Washburne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elihu_B._Washburne "Elihu B. Washburne") served as secretary of state for less than two weeks before becoming [ambassador to France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ambassadors_of_the_United_States_to_France "List of ambassadors of the United States to France").

A **82ª cerimônia dos Prêmios Globo de Ouro** foi realizada em **5 de janeiro de 2025**, no Beverly Hilton, em Los Angeles (EUA), com apresentação da comediante **Nikki Glaser** — primeira mulher a comandar o evento sozinha na história da premiação. ### 🎤 Melhor Stand-up para TV
**Ali Wong** por *Single Lady* (Netflix)
- Jamie Foxx — What Had Happened Was

---

## 🎯 QUEM LEVOU MAIS DE UM PRÊMIO

Alguns destaques marcaram a noite conquistando **mais de uma estatueta**:

| Produção | Prêmios | Categoria(s) |
|---|---|---|
| **🍿 Emilia Pérez** (filme) | **4 prêmios** | Melhor Filme — Musical/Comédia · Melhor Filme — Língua Não Inglesa · Melhor Atriz Coadjuvante (Zoe Saldaña) · Melhor Canção Original ("El Mal") |
| **🗡️ Xógum: A Gloriosa Saga do Japão** (série) | **4 prêmios** | Melhor Série — Drama · Melhor Ator (Hiroyuki Sanada) · Melhor Atriz (Anna Sawai) · Melhor Ator Coadjuvante (Tadanobu Asano) |
| **💥 O Brutalista** (filme) | **3 prêmios** | Melhor Filme — Drama · Melhor Ator (Adrien Brody) · Melhor Direção (Brady Corbet) |
| **🐰 Bebê Rena** (minissérie) | **2 prêmios** | Melhor Minissérie · Melhor Atriz Coadjuvante (Jessica Gunning) |
| **🪙 Hacks** (série) | **2 prêmios** | Melhor Série — Comédia/Musical · Melhor Atriz (Jean Smart) |

> ⚠️ Curiosidade: *Emilia Pérez*, apesar de ter sido a maior estrela da premiação com 10 indicações (recorde histórico para comédias/musicais), terminou com 4 vitórias — superada apenas por *Shōgun* entre as séries. Já *O Brutalista* ficou logo atrás com 3 estatuetas. No lado da TV, *O Urso*, que liderou em indicações (5), acabou ficando com apenas 1 prêmio.

---

**Resumo geral:** Os maiores vencedores foram **Emilia Pérez** (4 prêmios em cinema) e **Xógum** (4 prêmios em TV), seguidos por **O Brutalista** (3 prêmios). Netflix dominou com 36 indicações totais entre cinema e TV, sendo a distribuidora mais premiada da noite. A premiação também celebrou marcos históricos como a primeira vitória de uma brasileira (Fernanda Torres), a primeira série não anglófona premiada em melhor filme musical/comédia e a primeira apresentação feminina solo na história do evento.

The **82nd Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony that honored [excellence in film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film") and [American television productions of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_American_television "2024 in American television"). The winners were revealed during the live telecast, airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streaming on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") on January 5, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-2) The event was hosted by comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser"), making her the first solo female host in Golden Globes history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3)

The nominations were announced live on December 9, 2024, at a [press conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_conference "Press conference") at [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") by actors [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut") and [Mindy Kaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindy_Kaling "Mindy Kaling"), following an introduction from Golden Globes president, Helen Hoenhe.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")*, with 10 nominations, became the most nominated comedy/musical film in [Golden Globes history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards#Superlatives "Golden Globe Awards"), just 1 shy of the overall record of 11, set by [Robert Altman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Altman "Robert Altman")'s [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") [satire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire_(film_and_television) "Satire (film and television)") *[Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_(film) "Nashville (film)")* in the drama category in [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/33rd_Golden_Globe_Awards "33rd Golden Globe Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-5) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* received the second-most in film with 7 nominations, followed by *[Conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave_(film) "Conclave (film)")* with 6.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-6) Additionally, *[The Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series) "The Bear (TV series)")* led the television nominations with 5, followed by *[Only Murders in the Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Murders_in_the_Building "Only Murders in the Building")* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* with 4 each.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

## Ceremony information

On August 28, 2024, comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser") was announced as the host for this year's ceremony, following last year's widely criticized host, comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3) She is the first woman to host the Golden Globes solo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) Glaser herself was nominated for [Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television") for her [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy special, *Nikki Glaser: Someday You'll Die*,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) but lost to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s *Ali Wong: Single Lady*.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-10)

The ceremony was held at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on January 5, 2025. It was broadcast live on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") of White Cherry Entertainment returned from last year to executive produce the ceremony, along with [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)

On December 3, 2024, it was announced that the two Lifetime Achievement Awards, which were not presented last year, would return this year; however, they were presented during an untelevised gala dinner on January 3, 2025, prior to the telecast, similar to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) The recipient of the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") was [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis"), while the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award") was awarded to [Ted Danson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Danson "Ted Danson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

*[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")* star [Karla Sofía Gascón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Sofía_Gascón "Karla Sofía Gascón") was the first [trans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") nominee for a Golden Globe motion picture acting category, for the [Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy") category.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-12) [Jacques Audiard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Audiard "Jacques Audiard"), the director and writer of the film, was one of the most nominated individuals, with a total of three nominations: [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"), [Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay"), and co-lyricist of [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song") nominee "[El Mal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Mal_(song) "El Mal (song)")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7) The composers and co-lyricists of the song, [Camille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_(French_singer) "Camille (French singer)") and [Clément Ducol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clément_Ducol "Clément Ducol"), tied Audiard for most nominated individuals. Aside from "El Mal", they were also jointly nominated for composing *Emilia Pérez*'s [Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Score") and an additional Best Original Song nominee: "[Mi camino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_camino "Mi camino")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

This year's nominations were tabulated by [KPMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPMG "KPMG"), the U.S. audit, tax, and advisory firm, taking over [Ernst & Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_&_Young "Ernst & Young") after fifty plus years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15) [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") received a total of 36 nominations between film and television, the most of any distributor.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

*Emilia Pérez* is the first non-English-language film (with some parts of English in the film) to win [Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")* is the first [Latvian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvian_language "Latvian language") film to win [Best Animated Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Animated Feature Film").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-17) [Fernanda Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Torres "Fernanda Torres") became the first [Brazilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Portuguese "Brazilian Portuguese") actress to win a Golden Globe in an acting category,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) as well as the first Brazilian, first [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") and first [Portuguese-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") actor to win the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) She acknowledged her mother [Fernanda Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Montenegro "Fernanda Montenegro")'s nomination, for *[Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Station_(film) "Central Station (film)")* (1998), in the same category at the [56th Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/56th_Golden_Globe_Awards "56th Golden Globe Awards").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18)

*Emilia Pérez* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* were the biggest winners of the night, for film and television, respectively, with four wins each.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* was the next biggest film recipient, with three wins; for television, *[Baby Reindeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_Reindeer "Baby Reindeer")* and *[Hacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacks_(TV_series) "Hacks (TV series)")* each won two.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19)

# [2401.07883] The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator

[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.07883) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1)
> Abstract:Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) has become one of the most popular paradigms for enabling LLMs to access external data, and also as a mechanism for grounding to mitigate against hallucinations. When implementing RAG you can face several challenges like effective integration of retrieval models, efficient representation learning, data diversity, computational efficiency optimization, evaluation, and quality of text generation. Given all these challenges, every day a new technique to improve RAG appears, making it unfeasible to experiment with all combinations for your problem. In this context, this paper presents good practices to implement, optimize, and evaluate RAG for the Brazilian Portuguese language, focusing on the establishment of a simple pipeline for inference and experiments. We explored a diverse set of methods to answer questions about the first Harry Potter book. To generate the answers we used the OpenAI's gpt-4, gpt-4-1106-preview, gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, and Google's Gemini Pro. Focusing on the quality of the retriever, our approach achieved an improvement of MRR@10 by 35.4% compared to the baseline. When optimizing the input size in the application, we observed that it is possible to further enhance it by 2.4%. Finally, we present the complete architecture of the RAG with our recommendations. As result, we moved from a baseline of 57.88% to a maximum relative score of 98.61%.

## Submission history

# The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator

*Leonardo Avila Rodrigo Castaldoni Pedro Gengo Celio Larcher Marcos Piau Pablo Costa Vinicius Caridá

email: {pfinardi, leonardo.bernardi.avila, castaldoniro, pedro.gengo.lourenco, celiolarcher, marcos.piau.vieira, pablo.botton.costa, vfcarida}@gmail.com  
∗ Both authors contributed equally to this research.

###### Abstract

Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) has become one of the most popular paradigms for enabling LLMs to access external data, and also as a mechanism for grounding to mitigate against hallucinations. When implementing RAG you can face several challenges like effective integration of retrieval models, efficient representation learning, data diversity, computational efficiency optimization, evaluation, and quality of text generation. Given all these challenges, every day a new technique to improve RAG appears, making it unfeasible to experiment with all combinations for your problem. In this context, this paper presents good practices to implement, optimize, and evaluate RAG for the Brazilian Portuguese language, focusing on the establishment of a simple pipeline for inference and experiments. We explored a diverse set of methods to answer questions about the first Harry Potter book. To generate the answers we used the OpenAI’s gpt-4, gpt-4-1106-preview, gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, and Google’s Gemini Pro. Focusing on the quality of the retriever, our approach achieved an improvement of MRR@10 by <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" intent=":literal" alttext="35.4\%" id="abstract1.m1"><semantics><mrow><mn>35.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">35.4\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 35.4%35.4\% compared to the baseline. When optimizing the input size in the application, we observed that it is possible to further enhance it by <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" alttext="2.4\%" display="inline" id="abstract1.m2"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.4\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 2.4%2.4\%. Finally, we present the complete architecture of the RAG with our recommendations. As result, we moved from a baseline of <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" alttext="57.88\%" display="inline" id="abstract1.m3"><semantics><mrow><mn>57.88</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">57.88\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 57.88%57.88\% to a maximum relative score of <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" alttext="98.61\%" intent=":literal" id="abstract1.m4"><semantics><mrow><mn>98.61</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98.61\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 98.61%98.61\%.

## 1 Introduction

The rise of Large Language Models (LLMs) has changed the way we approach Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications. Their ability to answer different user queries in different domains allow these models to show a notable performance in a wide range of tasks like translation, summarizing, question answering, and many others [[1](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib1 "")]. However, there are a lot of open challenges when it comes to problems that require answers based on updated information, and external data, that were not available in the training data.

In order to overcome this challenge, a technique called Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) [[2](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib2 "")] was developed. This approach aims to solve the limitation of the need for external data, by fetching and incorporating this information in the prompt. With this, the model can generate more cohesive answers about subjects and data not seen during the training, decreasing the occurrence of hallucinations [[3](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib3 "")]. Nevertheless, this approach adds a new layer of challenges since it requires the development of a trustworthy retriever pipeline, given that the quality of the final answer can be highly affected if the retrieved text is not relevant to the user query [[4](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib4 "")].

The landscape of RAG is rapidly expanding, with a constant influx of new papers introducing diverse implementations [[5](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib5 "")]. Each of these variants proposes technical modifications or enhancements, such as different retrieval mechanisms, augmentation techniques, or fine-tuning methodologies. This proliferation, while a testament to the field’s dynamism, presents a substantial challenge for AI practitioners. The task of methodically experimenting with, and critically evaluating, each variant’s performance, scalability, and applicability becomes increasingly complex.

In this paper, we present a comprehensive series of experiments focused on the application of RAG specifically tailored for Brazilian Portuguese. Our research delves into evaluating various retrieval techniques, including both sparse and dense retrievers. Additionally, we explore two chunking strategies (naive and sentence window) to optimize the integration of retrieved information into the generation process. We also investigate the impact of the positioning of documents within the prompt, analyzing how this influences the overall quality and relevance of the generated content. Finally, our experiments extend to comparing the performance of different LLMs, notably GPT-4 and Gemini, in their ability to effectively incorporate the retrieved information and produce coherent, contextually accurate responses. This paper aims to provide valuable insights and practical guidelines for implementing RAG in Brazilian Portuguese.

Our main contributions are summarized as follows: 1) we propose a methodology to prepare a dataset in a format that allows quantifying the quality of the different steps in an RAG system. 2) We proposed a metric (maximum relative score) that allow us to direct quantify the existent gap between each approach and a perfect RAG system. 3) We discuss and compare different implementations, showing good practices and optimizations that can be used when developing a RAG system.

## 2 Data Preparation

The chosen dataset was the first Harry Potter book in its Brazilian Portuguese version. This choice is motivated since it is a well known book, and both the Gemini Pro and OpenAI models can answer general questions on the subject. Additionally, over the application of the standard ChatGPT tokenizer cl100k_base, we observed that there are approximately <!-- MathML: <math alttext="140,000" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S2.p1.m1"><semantics><mn>140,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">140,000</annotation></semantics></math> --> 140,000140,000 tokens in total, allowing the creation of prompts containing the entire book. Following, a dataset consisting of questions and corresponding answers was developed, with both question and answer generated by the gpt-4 model and based on a reference chunk.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1/pics/dataprep.png)Figure 1: From a large document (book), chunks were created, and for each chunk, a question and an answer were generated using gpt-4, where the answer is contained within the chunk.

Figure [1](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S2.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ 2 Data Preparation ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator") shows the data preparation process. Initially, the dataset was break into chunks with <!-- MathML: <math alttext="1000" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S2.p2.m1"><semantics><mn>1000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1000</annotation></semantics></math> --> 10001000 tokens each, without overlapping, resulting in <!-- MathML: <math alttext="140" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S2.p2.m2"><semantics><mn>140</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">140</annotation></semantics></math> --> 140140 chunks. Then, using the prompt described in Appendix [A](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#A1 "Appendix A PROMPTS ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator"), a <!-- MathML: <math alttext="\{question,answer\}" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S2.p2.m3"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{question,answer\}</annotation></semantics></math> --> {q​u​e​s​t​i​o​n,a​n​s​w​e​r}\{question,answer\} pair was created for each chunk in the style of the SQuAD dataset [[6](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib6 "")], meaning that the answer to the question is present within the reference text (chunk).

## 3 How to Evaluate

The contextual comparison of two text samples is not a straightforward task. For instance, despite the sentence<!-- MathML: <math alttext="{}_{1}=" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S3.p1.m1"><semantics><mrow><msub><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_{1}=</annotation></semantics></math> --> 1={}_{1}= "Brazil has won 5 FIFA World Cup titles.", and sentence<!-- MathML: <math alttext="{}_{2}=" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S3.p1.m2"><semantics><mrow><msub><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_{2}=</annotation></semantics></math> --> 2={}_{2}= "Brazil is the five-time champion of the FIFA World Cup." (both sentences translated into English for convenience) convey the same meaning, traditional metrics such as BLEU [[7](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib7 "")] and ROUGE [[8](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib8 "")] score may not be able to capture such similarity. Specifically, for the example cited:

- •     BLEU score <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" intent=":literal" alttext="[\text{sentence}_{1},\text{sentence}_{2}]=0.33" id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m1"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mtext>sentence</mtext><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mtext>sentence</mtext><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.33</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\text{sentence}_{1},\text{sentence}_{2}]=0.33</annotation></semantics></math> --> [sentence1,sentence2]=0.33[\text{sentence}_{1},\text{sentence}_{2}]=0.33

- •     ROUGE score <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" display="inline" alttext="[\text{sentence}_{1},\text{sentence}_{2}]=0.22" id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m1"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mtext>sentence</mtext><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mtext>sentence</mtext><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.22</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\text{sentence}_{1},\text{sentence}_{2}]=0.22</annotation></semantics></math> --> [sentence1,sentence2]=0.22[\text{sentence}_{1},\text{sentence}_{2}]=0.22

Therefore, an approach widely used in the literature is to employ gpt-4 to provide a score based on a given prompt, a concept similar to what was done in the G-Eval work [[9](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib9 "")]. In this work, a scoring system divided into <!-- MathML: <math alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S3.p3.m1"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> --> 55 categories to compare two texts was devised, with scores defined as following (translated into English for convenience):

- •     score 1: The answer has no relation to the reference.

- •     score 3: The answer has little relevance but is not aligned with the reference.

- •     score 5: The answer has moderate relevance but contains inaccuracies.

- •     score 7: The answer is aligned with the reference but has minor omissions.

- •     score 10: The answer is completely accurate and aligns perfectly with the reference.

The prompt used in the evaluation is shown in Appendix [A](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#A1 "Appendix A PROMPTS ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator"). Our approach uses a one-shot technique for each scoring category. Although, we believe that the evaluation could become more robust and deterministic with the addition of more few-shot examples for each scoring category, these possible variations were not explored in this work.

### 3.1 Relative Maximum Score

In order to assess performance variation for the followings experiments, we created a metric called the relative maximum score, which corresponds to the score given by a model when evaluating the correct combination of question and chunk for all pairs of a given dataset. Through this approach, it is possible to obtain the maximum score that an evaluated LLM could reach for a RAG system.

The Table [1](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S3.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 3.1 Relative Maximum Score ‣ 3 How to Evaluate ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator") presents results for the custom dataset created in Section [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S2 "2 Data Preparation ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator"), by using different LLMs to generate the answer and the gpt-4 score system previously defined.

Table 1: Relative maximum score in <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" alttext="140" display="inline" id="S3.T1.m2"><semantics><mn>140</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">140</annotation></semantics></math> --> 140140 questions from the created QA Harry Potter dataset.

Despite configuring all the seeds and reusing the prompts, the relative maximum in our data was approximately <!-- MathML: <math alttext="7.4" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S3.SS1.p3.m1"><semantics><mn>7.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.4</annotation></semantics></math> --> 7.47.4 average points. This points out that, even with a perfect retriever strategy, the RAG system is not able to achieve a perfect score in this dataset by using these LLM models.

For now on, all experiments in this study were assessed in terms of both the relative maximum and the percentage degradation with respect to the relative maximum, as defined in Equation [1](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S3.E1 "In 3.1 Relative Maximum Score ‣ 3 How to Evaluate ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator").

| <!-- MathML: <math display="block" intent=":literal" alttext="\text{degradation score}=1-\frac{\text{experiment score}}{\text{relative maximum}}" id="S3.E1.m1"><semantics><mrow><mtext>degradation score</mtext><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mtext>experiment score</mtext><mtext>relative maximum</mtext></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{degradation score}=1-\frac{\text{experiment score}}{\text{relative maximum}}</annotation></semantics></math> --> degradation score=1−experiment scorerelative maximum\text{degradation score}=1-\frac{\text{experiment score}}{\text{relative maximum}} | (1) |
| --- | --- |

With this score, we are able to address the problems regarding the retriever system itself, instead of having a vague idea of where is the main gap of our pipeline.

## 4 Introductory Experiments

In this section, we will establish a baseline for the metrics defined in Section [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S3 "3 How to Evaluate ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator"). Additionally, we will apply techniques of lower complexity and compare the results with the baseline. It’s worth noting that we did not explore prompt engineering techniques, although we are aware that prompt engineering has a direct impact on performance, as demonstrated in [[10](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib10 "")].

### 4.1 Baseline: no context

We are aware that LLMs are trained on a massive dataset that covers virtually the entire web. This circumstance, coupled with the popularity of the Harry Potter universe, forms a robust hypothesis for testing questions in isolation on OpenAI models. The answer for basic questions such as "Who is Harry Potter?", "Who killed Dumbledore?", and "What are Harry Potter’s main friends?", ChatGPT were correctly answered with precision. However, we observed that when dealing with more detailed questions, the performance was only reasonable. Below are two examples of detailed questions (translated into English for convenience):

- •
      Query: What was Harry’s strategy to stop Quirrell from focusing on the mirror and what did he try to do to discover the location of the Philosopher’s Stone?

  - –         Answer: What occurred to Harry was to keep Quirrell talking to stop him from focusing on the mirror.

- •
      Query: What model of broom did Harry Potter receive and who mentioned the special circumstances to Professor Flitwick?

  - –         Answer: The model of the broom that Harry Potter received is a Nimbus 2000 and it was Professor. Minerva who mentioned the special circumstances to Professor Flitwick.

The Table [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S4.T2 "Table 2 ‣ 4.1 Baseline: no context ‣ 4 Introductory Experiments ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator") shows the baseline results obtained using some known LLMs for the 140 questions built as described in section [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S2 "2 Data Preparation ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator") and evaluated as described in section [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S3 "3 How to Evaluate ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator"). For this task, no retrieved context were used, only the question.

Table 2: Performance of the External Knowledge experiment.

### 4.2 Long Context

In comparison to the GPT <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" intent=":literal" alttext="1" id="S4.SS2.p1.m1"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> --> 11 and <!-- MathML: <math alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S4.SS2.p1.m2"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> --> 22 models [[11](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib11 ""), [12](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib12 "")], which handle up to <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" alttext="1024" display="inline" id="S4.SS2.p1.m3"><semantics><mn>1024</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1024</annotation></semantics></math> --> 10241024 input tokens, the gpt-4-1106-preview model stands out for its remarkable ability to process up to 128k input tokens. This represents an approximately <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" display="inline" alttext="128" id="S4.SS2.p1.m4"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math> --> 128128 times increase in input capacity over just four years in model development.

The specific architecture of gpt-4 has not been disclosed, but it is believed that this model has not been pre-trained with a 128k token input context [[13](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib13 "")]. Perhaps a post-pre-training technique could have been used, which would have made it possible to expand the number of input tokens [[14](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib14 ""), [15](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib15 "")]. However, it is essential to note that such a technique may show degradation as the expansion limit is reached [[16](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib16 "")]. Similar to Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), which theoretically have an infinite context, disregarding performance limitations and vanish-gradients, we are interested in evaluating the performance of gpt-4-1106-preview over its 128k tokens.

To assess the impact of the gpt-4-1106-preview full context capacity on the model’s response, we proceed with a similar analysis of "Lost in The Middle" [[17](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib17 "")] in our dataset. This analysis explores the model output for a given question while changing the position of the answer throughout the prompt.
To conduct this experiment, the depth of the chunk containing the answer for the question was altered in increments of <!-- MathML: <math alttext="10\%" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S4.SS2.p3.m1"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 10%10\% of the total number of tokens in the context’s prompt. Thus, on the y-axis, there are <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" alttext="11" display="inline" id="S4.SS2.p3.m2"><semantics><mn>11</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11</annotation></semantics></math> --> 1111 variations of answer depth, represented by <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" alttext="{0\%,10\%,20\%,\dots,90\%,100\%}" intent=":literal" id="S4.SS2.p3.m3"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>90</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{0\%,10\%,20\%,\dots,90\%,100\%}</annotation></semantics></math> --> 0%,10%,20%,…,90%,100%{0\%,10\%,20\%,\dots,90\%,100\%}, and the x-axis represents the quantity of tokens used as input in the context, as shown in Figure [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S4.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 4.2 Long Context ‣ 4 Introductory Experiments ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator"). The colors represents the experiment score, where the greener the better.

## 5 Advanced Experiments

The studies and experiments outlined in section [4](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S4 "4 Introductory Experiments ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator") have shown unsatisfactory performance, marked by a degradation of at least <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" intent=":literal" alttext="20\%" id="S5.p1.m1"><semantics><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 20%20\% compared to the peak relative performance. Therefore, in this section, we explore various retrieval approaches for the RAG, recognizing that the quality of the retriever is a crucial factor in enhancing performance for this type of problem. We conducted an evaluation covering both sparse and dense search, a hybrid method, and even a multi-stage architecture using a reranker.

In pursuit of code debugging flexibility and easier customization at each stage, we chose not to utilize an RAG framework (like LangChain or Llama-Index). For a comprehensive guide on debugging RAG and more details about retrieval systems, refer to [[20](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib20 "")] and [[21](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib21 "")].

### 5.1 Retrievers

When deploying retrieval systems, it is essential to achieve a balance between “effectiveness” (How good are the results returned?) and “efficiency” (How much time it takes to return the results? or How much resources are used in terms of disk/RAM/GPU?). This balance ensures that latency, result quality, and computational budget remain within our application’s required limits. This work will exclusively focus on effectiveness measures to quantify the retrievers methods quality.

In our retriever experiments, the evaluation strategy centers around assessing how well the retriever performs in retrieving relevant information based on each given query <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" intent=":literal" alttext="q_{i}" id="S5.SS1.p2.m1"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> --> qiq_{i}. To achieve this, we employ the concept of recall. It is defined as the fraction of the relevant documents for a given query <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" alttext="q_{i}" display="inline" id="S5.SS1.p2.m2"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> --> qiq_{i} that are successfully retrieved in a ranked list <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" alttext="R" intent=":literal" id="S5.SS1.p2.m3"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> --> RR [[21](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib21 "")]. This metric is based on binary relevance judgments, assuming that documents are either relevant or not [[21](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib21 "")]. In this paper, each chunk is considered a document and only the respective chunk <!-- MathML: <math alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S5.SS1.p2.m4"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> --> did_{i} is considered relevant to the query <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" intent=":literal" alttext="q_{i}" id="S5.SS1.p2.m5"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> --> qiq_{i}. While recall is easy to interpret, it does not consider the specific rank positions in which the relevant chunk appears in <!-- MathML: <math alttext="R" intent=":literal" display="inline" id="S5.SS1.p2.m6"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> --> RR.

To overcome this limitation, we introduce Reciprocal Rank (RR) into our analysis. In this metric, the rank of the first relevant document to the query in <!-- MathML: <math alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S5.SS1.p3.m1"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> --> RR is used to compute the RR score [[21](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib21 "")]. Therefore, Reciprocal Rank offers a more nuanced evaluation by assigning a higher value when the relevant chunk is returned in the early positions of our retrievers given the respective query.

Recall and Reciprocal Rank were evaluated at a specific cutoff so the measures are presented as R@k and MRR@k. For each query, its results are evaluated and their mean serves as an aggregated measure of effectiveness of a given retriever method. The retrievers are introduced below.

In the category of sparse retrievers, we emphasize the BM25, a technique grounded in statistical weighting to assess relevance between search terms and documents. BM25 employs a scoring function that takes into account term frequency and document length, offering an efficient approach for retrieving pertinent information and is typically used as a strong baseline. However, it is exact-match based and can be powerless when query and document are relevant to each other but has no common words.

On the other hand, when exploring dense retrievers, we often encounter approaches based on the called bi-encoder design [[22](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib22 "")]. The bi-encoder independently encodes queries and documents, creating separate vector representations before calculating similarity. An advantage of this approach is that it can be initialized ‘offline’: document embeddings can be precomputed, leaving only the query embedding being calculated at search time, reducing latency.

The hybrid search technique aims to leverage the best of both sparse and dense search approaches. Given a question, both searches are conducted in parallel, generating two lists of candidate documents to answer it. The challenge then lies in combining the two results in the best possible way, ensuring that the final hybrid list surpasses the individual searches. Essentially, we can conceptualize it as a voting system, where each searcher casts a vote on the relevance of a document to a given query, and in the end, the opinions are combined to produce a better result.

The multi-stage search architecture is based on the retrieve-and-rerank pipeline. In the first stage, a retriever with good recall is typically used to perform an initial filtering of the documents to be returned. From this narrowed-down list, these candidate documents are then sent to a second stage, which involves higher computational complexity, to rerank them and enhance the final effectiveness of the system.

Next, we provide more details about each retriever used.

#### 5.1.1 BM25

Due to the user-friendly nature of BM25, its inclusion as a retriever method is always a welcome addition in RAG evaluations. A study that aligns with the same reasoning, albeit for a different application, can be found in [[23](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib23 "")], which illustrates the benefits of employing this algorithm to establish a robust baseline. Given that our data shares similarities with the SQuAD dataset, it is expected that many words from the query would be present in the chunk, contributing to the favorable effectiveness of BM25.

In the BM25 ranking function, <!-- MathML: <math alttext="k_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m1"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> --> k1k_{1} and <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" intent=":literal" alttext="b" id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m2"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> --> bb are parameters shaping term saturation and document length normalization, respectively. The BM25 formula integrates these parameters to score the relevance of a document to a query, offering flexibility in adjusting <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" display="inline" alttext="k_{1}" id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m3"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> --> k1k_{1} and <!-- MathML: <math alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m4"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> --> bb for improving effectiveness in different retrieval scenarios.

Pyserini’s BM25 implementation incorporates an analyzer with preprocessing steps such as stemming and language-specific stop word removal. For the sake of comparison, we included results obtained using rank-bm25 [[24](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib24 "")], a basic implementation without preprocessing that is widely used in Python and integrated into libraries like LangChain and Llama-index. OpenAI does not disclose extensive details about the ADA-002 architecture; however, we employed this model in retrieval as the presented bi-encoder design (Figure [5](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S5.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ 5.1.2 ADA-002 ‣ 5.1 Retrievers ‣ 5 Advanced Experiments ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator")): vector representations were constructed for all available chunks, and for each input query, its embedding was computed at search time. #### 5.1.3 Custom ADA-002

The Custom ADA-002 approach was also utilized in the dense retriever configuration presented in Section [5.1.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S5.SS1.SSS2 "5.1.2 ADA-002 ‣ 5.1 Retrievers ‣ 5 Advanced Experiments ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator"). However, embedding customization played a key role in our attempt to enhance the overall representation.

Embedding customization is not limited solely to OpenAI’s embeddings; it is a technique applicable to other embeddings of the same kind. There is a significant variety of approaches to optimize a matrix, with one of them being the application of Multiple Negative Ranking Loss, as presented in the article "Efficient Natural Language Response Suggestion for Smart Reply," Section 4.4 [[26](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib26 "")]. However, given our current focus on simplicity, we will reserve the exploration of this technique for future work. At this moment, we choose to utilize the Mean Squared Error (MSE) Loss.

#### 5.1.5 Reranker

The fundamental idea underlying multi-stage ranking is to divide document ranking into a sequence of stages. After an initial retrieval, which usually involves a sparse retriever or dense retriever, each subsequent stage re-evaluates and reranks the set of candidates forwarded from the preceding stage. Figure [9](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S5.F9 "Figure 9 ‣ 5.1.5 Reranker ‣ 5.1 Retrievers ‣ 5 Advanced Experiments ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator") represents a multi-stage pipeline where Pyserini BM25 performs the first stage and the candidate chunks are then re-evaluated by the reranker. After that, the final reranked list called retrieved chunks is presented as final result formed by <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" display="inline" alttext="k" id="S5.SS1.SSS5.p1.m1"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> --> kk chunks.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1/pics/reranker.png)Figure 9: Reranker Pipeline

Transformers-based models are commonly employed as rerankers, leveraging their capability to enhance the effectiveness of information retrieval systems by capturing intricate relationships and contextual information within documents and queries.

The initial utilization of transformers within a multi-stage ranking framework was presented in the study [[28](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib28 "")]. Their proposed model, known as monoBERT, transforms the ranking process into a relevance classification problem. It achieves this by sorting texts based on the conditional probability <!-- MathML: <math alttext="P(\text{Relevant}=1\,|\,d_{i};q)" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S5.SS1.SSS5.p3.m1"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext>Relevant</mtext><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0.170em">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>;</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(\text{Relevant}=1\,|\,d_{i};q)</annotation></semantics></math> --> P⁡(Relevant=1|di;q)P(\text{Relevant}=1\,|\,d_{i};q), where <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" alttext="q" intent=":literal" id="S5.SS1.SSS5.p3.m2"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> --> qq is the query and <!-- MathML: <math alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S5.SS1.SSS5.p3.m3"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> --> did_{i} represents documents [[21](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib21 "")]. The model simultaneously processes both queries and documents. This simultaneous processing leads to a more enriched interaction between them, often resulting in improved effectiveness [[29](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib29 "")], [[30](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib30 "")]. However, this neural models have a substantial number of parameters and the scoring of query-document pairs occurs at inference time. This, in turn, increases computational costs and latency. This kind of model is also known by cross-encoder. Refer to Figure [10](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S5.F10 "Figure 10 ‣ 5.1.5 Reranker ‣ 5.1 Retrievers ‣ 5 Advanced Experiments ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator") for an illustration of the query-document pair processing.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1/pics/cross_encoder.png)Figure 10: Cross-Encoder

In the other hand, monoT5 is a sequence-to-sequence reranker [[31](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib31 "")] that uses T5 models [[32](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib32 "")] to generate relevance scores between a pair of query and document. T5 models treat all tasks as text-to-text, requiring some adaptations for the query/document similarity task. During training, the format 'Query: {query} Document: {document} Relevant:' is used, with labels yes if the document is relevant to the query, and no otherwise. At inference time, the same format as the training data is used to format pairs of queries and documents to feed the model, and a single-token greedy decode is performed. The score is then obtained by calculating the softmax value considering only the tokens no and yes, and selecting the value corresponding to the yes token. Note that the tokens no and yes are the tokens used in the version provided by [[33](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib33 "")], but the publication that introduced the monoT5 architecture, [[31](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib31 "")], uses the tokens false and true. Figure [11](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S5.F11 "Figure 11 ‣ 5.1.5 Reranker ‣ 5.1 Retrievers ‣ 5 Advanced Experiments ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator") contains an illustration of the monoT5 architecture’s inference process.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1/pics/monot5.png)Figure 11: monoT5’s inference process

In our experiments, Pyserini BM25 was employed as first-stage retrieval, retrieving 50 documents to be reranked in the second stage. In the second stage, we utilized the model unicamp-dl/mt5-base-en-pt-msmarco-v2, a sequence-to-sequence reranker trained on pairs of queries and documents in English and Portuguese from the dataset [[33](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#bib.bib33 "")].

## 6 Conclusions

The implementation of RAG systems faces challenges such as the effective integration of retrieval models, efficient representation learning, the diversity of data, the optimization of computational efficiency, evaluation, and text generation quality. Faced with these constantly evolving obstacles, this article proposes best practices for the implementation, optimization, and evaluation of RAG on a Brazilian Portuguese dataset, focusing on a simplified pipeline for inference and experimentation.

So far, we have introduced the main components and methods along with their results and gaps. In this section, we will discuss key points that contribute to the performance improvement in RAG applications. We will start by discussing the relationship between the quality of the retriever and the achieved performance, in which our approach showed a significant improvement of MRR@10 by <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" display="inline" alttext="35.4\%" id="S6.p2.m1"><semantics><mrow><mn>35.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">35.4\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 35.4%35.4\% compared to the baseline. Next, we will address the impact of input size on performance. In this domain, we observed that it is possible to enhance the best information retrieval strategy by <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" intent=":literal" alttext="2.4\%" id="S6.p2.m2"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.4\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 2.4%2.4\% through input size optimization. Finally, we will present the complete architecture of RAG with our recommendations. When evaluating the final accuracy of our approach, we reached <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" display="inline" alttext="98.61\%" id="S6.p2.m3"><semantics><mrow><mn>98.61</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98.61\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 98.61%98.61\%, representing an improvement of <!-- MathML: <math alttext="40.73" intent=":literal" display="inline" id="S6.p2.m4"><semantics><mn>40.73</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40.73</annotation></semantics></math> --> 40.7340.73 in less degradation score compared to the baseline.

### 6.3 Final Results

Despite this work being grounded in a single dataset, it is always crucial to emphasize the importance of data quality. In a simplified manner, as illustrated in Figure [13](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S6.F13 "Figure 13 ‣ 6.3 Final Results ‣ 6 Conclusions ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator"), data quality in RAG can be divided into Input, Retriever, and Evaluation.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1/pics/core_points_RAG.png)Figure 13: Core Points in RAG.

- •     Input: How are the queries formulated? Are they synthetic or generic? What is the application’s purpose? Building a RAG for a chatbot differs significantly from constructing a RAG for extracting information from a long and complex document.

- •     Retriever: How do the data behave in information retrieval? Are the queries strongly linked by keywords in the text? What is the cosine similarity of query-to-query, query-to-document, and document-to-document?

- •     Evaluation: How are the data measured? Defining metrics and success rates, as in the first experiment, is always a safe path to avoid biases. Build the evaluation system before testing, avoiding bias.

In conclusion, the main contribution of this work was to identify and present the best possible configuration of techniques and parameters for a RAG application. Figure [14](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#S6.F14 "Figure 14 ‣ 6.3 Final Results ‣ 6 Conclusions ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator") provides a summarized overview of the end-to-end experiment results for the discussed approaches, and the best practices recommended by this study achieve a final accuracy of <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" intent=":literal" alttext="98.61\%" id="S6.SS3.p3.m1"><semantics><mrow><mn>98.61</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98.61\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 98.61%98.61\%, representing an improvement of <!-- MathML: <math alttext="40.73" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S6.SS3.p3.m2"><semantics><mn>40.73</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40.73</annotation></semantics></math> --> 40.7340.73 percentage points compared to the baseline.

## Appendix B Sentence Window

There are a wide variety of techniques available for dealing with RAG and new approaches are constantly emerging. In this work we highlight the main existing strategies, although we have also explored others, such as the RAG Sentence Window approach.

The sentence window chunk constitutes a strategy embedded in the llama-index11 1 <https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/examples/node_postprocessor/MetadataReplacementDemo.html>, which employs the small-to-large approach. The entire chunk retrieval process is based on cosine similarity. Initially, a single sentence is retrieved, followed by expanding (window) around the retrieved sentence to construct a more extensive chunk. This method implies that the most relevant context is always centered and retrieved first, as opposed to being at the edges of a chunk boundary. Figure [15](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#A2.F15 "Figure 15 ‣ Appendix B Sentence Window ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator") illustrates the comparison between naive chunks and those obtained through the "sentence window" strategy.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1/pics/sentence-window_chunk_2.png)Figure 15: Comparison between the naive chunking and small to big strategies, where the latter initially retrieves a single sentence and then performs windowing with padding on both sides.

Despite being a promising technique, the results on our dataset were inferior to the naive strategy, as indicated in Table [9](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1#A2.T9 "Table 9 ‣ Appendix B Sentence Window ‣ The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator").

Table 9: Performance of the RAG Sentence Window.

Our hypothesis for the low performance includes:

1. 1.     The construction of the question and answer occurred after the "chunk" cut, so there is no answer between two chunks.

2. 2.     Embedding sentence by sentence in the Harry Potter book causes ambiguity: there are multiple sentences with the name Harry Potter, which adds a significant challenge to the step of retrieving the correct sentence.
